title: California Community Profiles
intro:
How does a place compare?

Pick a type of jurisdiction, then select a place by name or on the map, and choose the dimensions you care about. Each profile compares the place with California as a whole, and splits key measures between land that is protected under the state’s 30x30 definition (GAP 1–2) and land that is not.

  • Park access — Who can walk to a park in 10 minutes, using the Trust for Public Land's ParkServe walk zones, and which neighborhoods are left out.
  • Health & equity — Park access, disadvantaged communities, and cumulative environmental burden (CalEnviroScreen).
  • Climate risk — Projected heat, flood and sea-level-rise exposure, recent wildfire and prescribed burns, and wildfire hazard.
  • Biodiversity — Species of Greatest Conservation Need, listed species, and critical habitat — and how much of it is protected.

All numbers are computed on demand from public datasets with fixed, reviewable SQL — no AI model is involved. Open “Method & SQL” under any panel to see exactly what ran.

statewide.label: California
statewide.aoi10: SELECT DISTINCT h0, h8, h10 FROM read_parquet('s3://public-ca30x30/ecoregion/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')

jurisdictions.label: Cities
jurisdictions.description: Incorporated cities and towns (2024 Census places)
jurisdictions.aoi: SELECT DISTINCT h3_cell_to_parent(c, 0) AS h0, c AS h8 FROM (SELECT unnest(h3_uncompact_cells(list(cell), 8)) AS c FROM read_parquet('{{SITE}}/data/aoi/city-r8.parquet') WHERE id = '{{ID}}')
jurisdictions.aoi10: SELECT DISTINCT h3_cell_to_parent(c, 0) AS h0, h3_cell_to_parent(c, 8) AS h8, c AS h10 FROM (SELECT unnest(h3_uncompact_cells(list(cell), 10)) AS c FROM read_parquet('{{SITE}}/data/aoi/city.parquet') WHERE id = '{{ID}}')
jurisdictions.cells10: SELECT DISTINCT GEOID AS id, h0, h10 FROM read_parquet('s3://public-census/census-2024/place/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') WHERE STATEFP = '06' AND CLASSFP LIKE 'C%'
jurisdictions.list: SELECT GEOID AS id, NAME AS name, CASE WHEN LSAD = '43' THEN 'town' ELSE 'city' END AS detail, ST_XMin(geom) AS xmin, ST_YMin(geom) AS ymin, ST_XMax(geom) AS xmax, ST_YMax(geom) AS ymax FROM read_parquet('s3://public-census/census-2024/place.parquet') WHERE STATEFP = '06' AND CLASSFP LIKE 'C%' ORDER BY NAME
